standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of an element generating the radical of the maximal ideal in a one-dimensional local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides g with m_A = radical of (g), which realizes L as the localization A_g.

standard_prerequisites.name: Zero-dimensional rings as products of localizations at minimal primes
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the identification L = A_g used to clear denominators.

core_obligations: Use Noetherianity to get I^t = 0 for some t > 0, and set up the inductive claim that for f = a + i with i in I^k L one can reach the image of A (proof lines 7616-7617).
Expand f^n = a^n + n a^{n-1} i modulo I^{k+1} L, reducing the problem to showing that n a^{n-1} i lies in the image of I^k -> I^k L for some large n (proof lines 7618-7620).
Choose g in A with m_A equal to the radical of (g) and conclude L = A_g, so that elements of L can be written with denominator a power of g (proof lines 7621-7623).

Use that a^n lies in (g) for large n, so multiplication by a high power of a clears denominators of elements of L, which gives the required divisibility and closes the induction (proof lines 7624-7626).
proof_roadmap: Filter the correction term by powers of I using nilpotency.
Expand a power of f and isolate the term to be controlled.
Realize L as a localization so denominators are powers of one element.
Clear denominators with a high power of the maximal-ideal element.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring A, if f in L = product of the localizations at the minimal primes is of the form f = i + a with a in the maximal ideal and i in I L (I being the intersection of the minimal primes), then some power of f lies in the image of A -> L. The proof uses nilpotency of I, sets up an induction on the exponent k measuring how deep the correction term lies, expands f^n = a^n + n a^{n-1} i modulo I^{k+1}L, and reduces to showing that n a^{n-1} i lies in the image of I^k for large n; this is achieved by choosing g with m_A = radical of (g), so that L = A_g, and using that a high power of a lies in (g), which lets one clear denominators (proof lines 7616-7626). H2: the induction through the I-adic filtration and the denominator-clearing step are the substance.
